cards.explanation: Pashhur has Jeremiah beaten and put in the stocks. He hears Jeremiah prophesying and has Jeremiah the prophet beaten and put in the stocks at the Upper Gate of Benjamin (Jeremiah 20:2). Pashhur is the chief official in the house of the LORD, so he's the one who should know better. I think this is a hard one to read, friends.

Jeremiah gives Pashhur a new name from the LORD. When Pashhur releases Jeremiah from the stocks, Jeremiah says to him, "The LORD does not call you Pashhur, but Magor-missabib." (Jeremiah 20:3). Jeremiah just spent a night in the stocks, and he still has the LORD's word to deliver, friends.

The word is terror. The LORD says, "I will make you a terror to yourself and to all your friends." (Jeremiah 20:4). That's what the name Magor-missabib is pointing to. It's a heavy word, so I'll say it plain: it's a hard thing to hear.

The answer is Babylon. The LORD says, "…I will hand Judah over to the king of Babylon…" (Jeremiah 20:4). That reaches past one man in the stocks, friends, since it's all of Judah being handed over. The message was never just about Pashhur.

Enemies will carry it all off. The LORD says He will give the wealth of this city to their enemies, and they will plunder it, seize it and carry it off to Babylon (Jeremiah 20:5). That includes all the treasures of the kings of Judah. Nothing on that list gets left behind, bakers.

The answer is True. The LORD says, "And you, Pashhur, and all who live in your house, will go into captivity." (Jeremiah 20:6). Notice that it's his whole house, not just him, friends. The word lands right on his own front door.

He will die and be buried in Babylon. The LORD says, "You will go to Babylon, and there you will die and be buried…" (Jeremiah 20:6). It's a sober ending, friends, and the text doesn't soften it. Pashhur goes to Babylon, and there he dies and is buried.

The answer is False. The LORD says Pashhur's friends are the ones "…to whom you have prophesied these lies." (Jeremiah 20:6). So what Pashhur prophesied to them was lies, not the truth, friends. I think that makes the stocks sit even heavier.
